cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What conflict took place in June-July 1999, after Vajpayee's bus journey to Lahore in February 1999?
cards.back: 1999 February: Indian PM Vajpayee undertakes bus journey to Lahore to sign a Peace Declaration June-July: Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan
cards.quote: 1999 February: Indian PM Vajpayee undertakes bus journey to Lahore to sign a Peace Declaration June-July: Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan
cards.note: The Kargil conflict took place in June-July 1999.
reasons: review:CONFLICT: Kargil conflict dated June-July on the timeline (Contemporary South Asia p.32) but May and June, with India recovering points by 26 July, in the detailed account (India's External Relations p.66). Keep the detailed account; the timeline card also repeats the Lahore card. (conflict sweep, 3

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: In what deeper sense are environment and resource issues political?
cards.back: All these raise the issue of who wields how much power. They are, therefore, deeply political questions.
cards.quote: All these raise the issue of who wields how much power. They are, therefore, deeply political questions.
reasons: review:Vague front; generic remark, not an exam fact

cards.front: What did the mid-1980s discovery of the ozone hole over the Antarctic reveal?

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: 1947 was the year of one of the largest, most abrupt, unplanned and tragic what in human history?
cards.back: The year 1947 was the year of one of the largest, most abrupt, unplanned and tragic transfer of population that human history has known.
cards.quote: The year 1947 was the year of one of the largest, most abrupt, unplanned and tragic transfer of population that human history has known.
reasons: review:Front is an open "what" with obvious synonyms (migration, displacement, mass exodus); NCERT word "transfer of population" is not forced.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What per cent of the eligible voters in the first general election were literate?
cards.back: At that time there were 17 crore eligible voters, who had to elect about 3,200 MLAs and 489 Members of Lok Sabha. Only 15 per cent of these eligible voters were literate.
cards.quote: At that time there were 17 crore eligible voters, who had to elect about 3,200 MLAs and 489 Members of Lok Sabha. Only 15 per cent of these eligible voters were literate.
reasons: review:Single statistic tied to one year (15 per cent literate in the first election); trivia, not a line to hold.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What came up in India after the experience of the Emergency?
cards.back: Many civil liberties organisations came up after this experience.
cards.quote: Many civil liberties organisations came up after this experience.
reasons: review:"What came up in India after the Emergency?" has many right answers (Janata government, protest movements, etc.); front does not single out civil liberties organisations. Also thin importance.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: By which year was the reorganisation of the North-East completed?
cards.back: The reorganisation of the North-East was completed by 1972.
cards.quote: The reorganisation of the North-East was completed by 1972.
reasons: review:CONFLICT: "Reorganisation of the North-East was completed by 1972" (Regional Aspirations p.127) is unqualified, but Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh became States only in 1987 (Regional Aspirations p.126, Nation-Building p.23). Keep the dated statehood cards. (conflict sweep, 31 Oct)

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: Finally, these cases make us appreciate the ____ of the makers of our Constitution in dealing with questions of diversity.
cards.back: Finally, these cases make us appreciate the farsightedness of the makers of our Constitution in dealing with questions of diversity.
cards.quote: Finally, these cases make us appreciate the farsightedness of the makers of our Constitution in dealing with questions of diversity.
reasons: review:Closing flourish, not a mark-carrying fact; blank has obvious synonyms (wisdom, foresight, vision), so no single right fill; 'must/good' is moot as the card is not worth memory.

cards.subject: political_science
cards.front: What did some critics contend after the demolition of the Ayodhya structure in 1992?
cards.back: In 1992, following the demolition of the structure, some critics contended that it presented a substantial challenge to the principles of Indian democracy.
cards.quote: In 1992, following the demolition of the structure, some critics contended that it presented a substantial challenge to the principles of Indian democracy.
reasons: review:Hedged 'some critics contended' line with an open-ended answer; a student cannot reproduce the exact wording and it is not a mark-carrying fact. Better as a key_line with a blank on a headed point.
